solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Grew old and silver before empty end

indicators.note: before places the silver ahead of what follows

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: empty means the word end loses its inside, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone grew old and grey-haired before an end that felt hollow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' strips the middle N from END, leaving ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense synonym: to have become elderly is to have aged.

clue.text: Terrible danger holding end of wartime bomb

indicators.note: holding means the scrambled letters wrap round the next piece
terrible suggests the letters of danger are wrecked and rearranged
end of picks the final letter of the word wartime

explanation.surface: A dreadful danger posed by a bomb from the war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible' rearranges DANGER; 'holding' puts the E that ends 'wartime' inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand-thrown explosive is a small kind of bomb.

clue.text: Avoid Italian magistrate imprisoning daughter

indicators.note: imprisoning means the magistrate's title encloses the next piece

parts.note: the Doge was the chief magistrate of Venice and Genoa

explanation.surface: Steer clear of an Italian official who has locked up a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to evade or sidestep something is to avoid it.

clue.text: Pushing down to remove trousers when embracing lust, perhaps

indicators.note: embracing means the trouser-removing word wraps round the next piece

parts.note: to debag is a British prank of pulling someone's trousers off
lust is one of the seven deadly sins, so an example of a sin

explanation.surface: A lewd scene of trousers being pulled down in a lustful clinch.
explanation.walkthrough: DEBAG is British schoolboy slang for removing someone's trousers as a prank.
explanation.definitionFit: Lowering in value or quality, degrading something, is pushing it down.

clue.text: Proper contest of honour avoided by learner

indicators.note: avoided by means the learner letter is left out of the contest

parts.note: a duel is a fight fought to settle a point of honour
L stands for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A learner sensibly sidesteps a proper duel.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective synonym: what is fitting or owed is rightful, appropriate.

clue.text: Tree bought initially by complete enthusiast

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word bought

parts.note: utter means complete, as in utter nonsense
a nut is an informal word for a fan, as in a fitness nut

explanation.surface: A tree purchased by someone utterly obsessed with trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A North American walnut species is called the white walnut or this tree.

clue.text: Quiet at home — greatly appreciate a lively party

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
in means at home, as in staying in
dig is slang for really liking something

explanation.surface: Someone who prefers quiet nights in still loves a good party.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal noun for a noisy celebration or knees-up.

clue.text: Hangman's rope shortly put over head of executed

indicators.note: put over in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: shortly means soon, before long

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of the word executed

explanation.surface: The hangman's rope will soon be slipped over the condemned man's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put over' reverses SOON to NOOS; then add E. 'Shortly' looks like it means abbreviate, but it is a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A looped rope used for hanging, tightened by a slipknot.

clue.text: School chief needs others for support

parts.note: the head is the headteacher in charge of a school
the rest means the others, the remainder

explanation.surface: The headteacher needs backing from the other staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A cushioned support for the back of the head, as on a car seat.

clue.text: One Conservative figure that's revered

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
Con is the abbreviation for a member of Britain's Conservative party

explanation.surface: A single Tory politician held up as a hero.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol or venerated person is someone worshipped or deeply admired.

clue.text: A DJ playing English rock

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of A DJ are moved around

explanation.surface: A disc jockey spinning English rock music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock' looks like a music genre but means a hard green stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A green semi-precious stone used in carvings and jewellery.

clue.text: Greatly involved, want to be in store for the future

indicators.note: to be in means the want word goes inside the storing word

parts.note: to keep something is to store it for later
want means need, lack

explanation.surface: Someone heavily committed, hoarding things for a rainy day.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: deeply immersed or thoroughly embroiled in a matter, as if wading.

clue.text: Like metro, travelling some distance

indicators.note: travelling suggests the letters are on the move, rearranged

explanation.surface: Riding the underground covers a fair way.
explanation.definitionFit: A metric unit of length, a thousand metres.

clue.text: Allowed Shakespeare's prince to be very destructive

parts.note: let means allowed, permitted
Prince Hal is the young Henry V in Shakespeare's Henry IV plays

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's prince is permitted to wreak havoc.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadly or capable of causing death, hence extremely damaging.

clue.text: Nut tree starting off a nursery rhyme?

definitions.meaning: a North American tree that bears hard edible nuts
the first word of ... Dickory Dock, the mouse-and-clock rhyme

explanation.surface: A tree with nuts that begins a children's song.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a nut-bearing tree and the opening word of a well-known nursery rhyme.

clue.text: Weapon returned to obtain some gold, perhaps

indicators.note: returned means the weapon word is read backwards

parts.note: a gun is a weapon
get means obtain

explanation.surface: A gun is given back in exchange for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A lump of precious metal, gold being the classic example.

clue.text: Being always superficial, blowing kiss

indicators.note: blowing as in blowing a kiss: the kiss is sent away, dropped from the word

parts.note: superficial means on the surface, outward
X stands for a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Someone forever shallow, always blowing kisses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blowing' takes the X out of EXTERNAL, as a blown kiss is sent off.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasting forever: something that exists for all time.

clue.text: Plate came mostly to be served up here

indicators.note: served up suggests the letters are dished out in a new order
mostly means the word came loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A plate turned up, almost ready for the food to be dished out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts CAME to CAM; 'to be served up' rearranges PLATE CAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A table mat is where a meal is set down, so 'here' points to it.

clue.text: Rent left, gaining freedom from worries

parts.note: ease means freedom from anxiety

explanation.surface: Paying rent leaves the tenant carefree.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to let or hire out property under contract.

clue.text: Stink when classical language gets its first cut

indicators.note: gets its first cut means the opening letter is chopped off

parts.note: Greek is one of the classical languages

explanation.surface: A smelly scene when the Greek class is cancelled.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to give off a strong foul smell.

clue.text: Replace Descartes, perhaps, with Watt

parts.note: René Descartes, the French philosopher, gives a first name
W is the symbol for watt, the unit of power

explanation.surface: Swapping the philosopher Descartes for the engineer Watt.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb sense: to restore or substitute something new for the old.

clue.text: Drop round for pudding

parts.note: sag means droop, drop
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Pop round for dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: A starchy dessert made from palm pith grains cooked in milk.

clue.text: Time showering, say, is something the coach provides

parts.note: raining is an example of weather that showers down

explanation.surface: Time in the showers comes after a coach's session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coach' suggests a bus but is a sports trainer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports coach's job is instruction and practice sessions.

clue.text: Everyone's name, not the initial

indicators.note: not the initial means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: to call someone something is to name them

explanation.surface: A name for everyone, without the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pronoun synonym: every person, the whole lot.

clue.text: Truly we will, I agree

parts.note: very is an old word for true or real, as in the very thing
the contraction of we will

explanation.surface: A firm promise: truly, we will.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe of the contraction is dropped in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase of assent, said when accepting a suggestion.

clue.text: Carnivore has to run back

indicators.note: back means the running word is read in reverse

parts.note: flow means run, as water runs

explanation.surface: A meat-eater has to retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild canine predator, a classic meat-eating animal.
